title: Income-tax Act, 1961
source: curated summary - authentic text at the India Code URL
note: Key sections for individual and corporate taxation, TDS, advance tax, assessments, appeals. Full Act has 298 sections + schedules.

sections.heading: Charge of income-tax
sections.text: Income-tax shall be charged for each assessment year at the rate or rates prescribed by a Central Act, on the total income of the previous year of every person.

sections.heading: Scope of total income
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the total income of any previous year of a person who is a resident includes all income from whatever source derived, whether received or deemed to be received in India, or accrues or arises to him outside India. For non-residents, only income received or deemed to be received in India, or accruing or arising in India.

sections.heading: Income deemed to accrue or arise in India
sections.text: The following incomes shall be deemed to accrue or arise in India: (i) all income accruing or arising, directly or indirectly, through or from any business connection in India, or through or from any property in India, or through or from any asset or source of income in India; (ii) salaries earned in India; (iii) dividends paid by Indian companies; (iv) interest payable by Government or a resident; (v) royalties and fees for technical services payable by a resident.

sections.heading: Incomes not included in total income
sections.text: In computing the total income of a previous year of any person, any income falling within the following clauses shall not be included: (10D) any sum received under a life insurance policy; (10(10D)) maturity proceeds of ULIP subject to conditions; (12A) payments from recognized provident fund; (13) payments from approved superannuation fund; (34) agricultural income; (38) long-term capital gains on equity shares/equity-oriented MFs (subject to STT).

sections.heading: Special provision for computation of total income of individual or HUF
sections.text: An individual or HUF may opt to be taxed at concessional slab rates without claiming specified deductions/exemptions (e.g., 80C, 80D, HRA, LTA). The option is available for assessment year 2021-22 onwards and can be switched once in a lifetime (for those with business income) or annually (for others).

sections.heading: Return of income
sections.text: Every person whose total income exceeds the basic exemption limit must furnish a return of income by the due date: 31 July for non-audit cases; 31 October for audit cases; 30 November for transfer pricing cases. Belated return can be filed up to 31 December of the assessment year, with fee under s.234F.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: Assessment types: (1) self-assessment under s.140A; (2) summary assessment under s.143(1) - intimation within 9 months of FY end; (3) scrutiny assessment under s.143(3) - after notice under s.143(2); (4) best judgment assessment under s.144 - for non-compliance; (5) income escaping assessment under s.147 - reopening within 4 years (10 years if income > Rs 50 lakh).

sections.heading: TDS on interest other than interest on securities
sections.text: Any person responsible for paying interest (other than on securities) to a resident shall deduct TDS at 10% (20% if no PAN) if aggregate interest exceeds Rs 40,000 (Rs 50,000 for senior citizens) in a FY. Applies to banks, co-operative societies, post offices.

sections.heading: TDS on fees for professional or technical services
sections.text: TDS at 10% (20% if no PAN) on fees for professional services (legal, medical, engineering, architectural, accountancy, technical consultancy, interior decoration) and technical services (managerial, technical, consultancy) if aggregate exceeds Rs 30,000 in a FY. Threshold for individuals/HUF is Rs 50,000.

sections.heading: Advance tax liability
sections.text: Every person whose estimated tax liability for the FY exceeds Rs 10,000 must pay advance tax in instalments: 15% by 15 June; 45% by 15 September; 75% by 15 December; 100% by 15 March. For eligible senior citizens (no business income), no advance tax required. Interest under s.234B (shortfall) and s.234C (deferment) applies.

sections.heading: Fee for default in furnishing return of income
sections.text: Fee for late filing: Rs 5,000 if return filed after due date but on or before 31 December of assessment year; Rs 10,000 otherwise. If total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, fee restricted to Rs 1,000.

sections.heading: Settlement Commission
sections.text: An assessee may apply to the Income-tax Settlement Commission for settlement of cases involving income escaping assessment or disputes on tax liability. Application admissible if additional tax liability exceeds Rs 5 lakh (or no limit for certain cases). Proceedings abate on rejection.

sections.heading: Revision of orders prejudicial to revenue
sections.text: The Principal Commissioner/Commissioner may revise any order of a subordinate authority if it is erroneous and prejudicial to revenue. Must give opportunity of hearing. Cannot revise if appeal is pending. Time limit: 2 years from end of FY in which order passed.

sections.heading: Penalty for concealment of income
sections.text: Penalty of 100% to 300% of tax sought to be evaded if the assessee has concealed income or furnished inaccurate particulars. The AO must record satisfaction that concealment was deliberate. Replaced by s.270A for assessments from AY 2017-18 onwards.

sections.heading: Penalty for under-reporting and misreporting of income
sections.text: Penalty for under-reporting: 50% of tax on under-reported income. Penalty for misreporting: 200% of tax on misreported income. Misreporting includes: suppression of facts, claim of expenditure not substantiated, false entry in books, failure to record receipt. No penalty if good faith bonafide belief shown.
